ladder.header: Historical maximum progress in any attempt; final state and task success are separate judgments.

levels.text:
Initial state before the gripper reaches the rope for the first pickup.
No useful arrival within grasping range of the rope has yet been positively observed.
Motion toward the rope while still far away does not establish S1.

The gripper reaches the rope's pickup location for the first manipulation cycle.
The gripper arrives within grasping range of a rope segment, visibly positioned to attempt pickup.
Physical contact and a successful grasp are not required.
An approach from afar or unrelated arm motion is insufficient.

The first pickup establishes a secure, controlled hold of the rope.
Across a visible interval, the same rope segment shows sustained control by moving coherently with the closed gripper through lift, tension, or translation.
Jaw closure, a brief pinch, brushing, or a nudge without sustained control does not establish holding.
Later loss of the grasp does not erase this historical milestone.

The held rope is brought into an insertion-ready orientation at the LEFT (FIRST) clip.
The controlled rope is at the LEFT (FIRST) clip mouth region.
The local rope segment is visibly oriented with that clip's insertion axis, primarily verified in WRIST-L.
Alignment far from the clip, empty-gripper alignment, and side-view overlap are insufficient.
No separate reach-the-clip stage or unengaged dwell interval is required.

The rope itself engages the LEFT (FIRST) clip mouth in an insertion-directed interaction.
The rope visibly contacts and begins entering under or into the LEFT (FIRST) clip lip, including partial insertion.
Contact with the table, the clip exterior, or the gripper alone does not establish engagement.
Engagement does not prove a persistent seat; seating remains a separate physical judgment.

The gripper lets go of the rope after the first-clip placement attempt.
A previously held rope segment becomes free of the jaws as they open or separate from it after work at the LEFT (FIRST) clip.
Timestamp the first supported loss of gripper retention, not merely the start of jaw opening.
The FIRST clip need not be successfully seated; this milestone records release, not placement quality.
An accidental slip from closed jaws or opening empty jaws is not a release.
A release during an initial pickup retry, before work at the FIRST clip, is not S5.
If this is also the episode's last release, it is still S5, not S10.

After the first-clip attempt, the gripper returns to the rope for the second pickup cycle.
A distinct return to the rope after work at the LEFT (FIRST) clip brings the gripper within grasping range of the segment to be acquired for the RIGHT (SECOND) clip.
The first clip does not need to be seated for the second cycle to begin.
Repeated grasp attempts before work at the FIRST clip remain first-cycle retries, not S6.
Continuing to transport the original held segment is not a new reach-to-pickup milestone.
Do not fabricate an earlier first-release timestamp if it was occluded.

The second pickup establishes a new secure, controlled hold of the rope.
A distinct second acquisition after the first-clip attempt establishes sustained gripper-coupled rope motion across a visible interval.
The new hold may be on the same or a different rope segment.
A missed close, transient pinch, or continuing the unchanged first hold is not S7.
The FIRST clip need not be seated; do not infer its state from the new grasp.

The held rope is brought into an insertion-ready orientation at the RIGHT (SECOND) clip.
The controlled rope is at the RIGHT (SECOND) clip mouth region.
WRIST-L positively establishes insertion-compatible orientation of the local rope segment relative to this clip.
The FIRST clip need not remain seated; second-cycle progress and first-clip outcome are separate.
Orientation while far from the clip, empty-gripper alignment, or projection overlap is insufficient.
If the rope was carried continuously between clips, do not invent S6 or S7.

The rope itself engages the RIGHT (SECOND) clip mouth in an insertion-directed interaction.
The rope visibly contacts and begins entering under or into the RIGHT (SECOND) clip lip, including partial insertion.
Engagement is not proof that either clip is fully seated.
Gripper-only contact, table contact, and merely hovering over the mouth are insufficient.
Do not require a successful first-clip seat to record an observed second-clip engagement.

The gripper lets go of the rope at the end of the second-clip placement attempt.
A previously held rope segment becomes free of the opening or separating jaws after work at the RIGHT (SECOND) clip.
This is the final relinquishment of the routing attempt, not a temporary release followed by another pickup in that attempt.
Release does not establish success: either clip may still be unseated.
Opening empty jaws or an accidental slip from closed jaws does not establish S10.
Ending the episode after only the first-clip release remains S5, not S10.
Timestamp actual loss of retention; do not wait for the gripper to retreat fully.

task_definition.displayName: Routing · left clip, then right clip
task_definition.objective: Seat and retain the rope in the LEFT clip first, then the RIGHT clip. A deliberate right-clip insertion attempt before left-clip seating is a terminal failure. Release is optional.
successCriteria: The LEFT physical clip must be fully seated before the first deliberate insertion attempt at the RIGHT physical clip. Right-first attempts are terminal wrong_clip_order failures even if both clips are later seated.
The rope is seated beneath the retaining features of both designated physical clips and remains captured in both at the end.
Gripper retention or release does not affect success. Contact or partial engagement is insufficient.
A high stage or final release does not prove both clips remain seated. First-clip loss during second-clip work is still failure.

entities.description: Single flexible rope or cable manipulated and tensioned by the robot.
Robot gripper and jaws used to acquire, transport, release, and optionally re-grasp the rope.
The fixed LEFT physical clip in the canonical workspace frame; always the first required target. Identify it jointly from the two opposing side views, not screen-left in an arbitrary camera.
The fixed RIGHT physical clip in the canonical workspace frame; always the second required target, regardless of visitation order or camera reversal.
The supporting pegboard and work surface on which the rope and two clips are arranged.

evidenceViews.description: Fixed side_1 view; combine it with SIDE-2 for global rope motion, clip identity, grasp control, and the end-to-end routing history.
caveats: One fixed side view does not cover the full rope and both clips reliably.
The clips are small and perspective overlap can make an unseated rope appear close to, over, or inside a clip.
SIDE-1 alone is not authoritative for the fine off-axis, beside, lip-engaged, or fully seated distinction.

evidenceViews.description: Fixed side_2 view opposing SIDE-1; combine both side views to follow the rope end-to-end and determine which clip is being attempted.
caveats: Its image-space left and right are not interchangeable with SIDE-1 because the cameras oppose one another.
The clips are small and perspective overlap can hide whether the rope is captured under a clip lip.
SIDE-2 alone is not authoritative for the fine seat and orientation geometry.

evidenceViews.description: Gripper-mounted wrist_left view that travels to the active clip; primary authority for local rope-versus-mouth orientation, lip engagement, and capture under the clip.
caveats: The wrist view cannot show both distant clips or the whole rope at once.
A wrist close-up near a clip does not prove that the rope is actually controlled by the gripper or identify the active clip without the side views.
Occlusion by the gripper or rope may make a boundary unresolvable; use the lower supported stage and request review rather than infer a seat.

stages.name: Rope not yet reached
stages.description: Initial state before the gripper reaches the rope for the first pickup.
entryCriteria: No useful arrival within grasping range of the rope has yet been positively observed.
exclusions: Motion toward the rope while still far away does not establish S1.

stages.name: Reach the rope
stages.description: The gripper reaches the rope's pickup location for the first manipulation cycle.
entryCriteria: The gripper arrives within grasping range of a rope segment, visibly positioned to attempt pickup.
exclusions: Physical contact and a successful grasp are not required.
An approach from afar or unrelated arm motion is insufficient.

stages.name: Hold the rope
stages.description: The first pickup establishes a secure, controlled hold of the rope.
entryCriteria: Across a visible interval, the same rope segment shows sustained control by moving coherently with the closed gripper through lift, tension, or translation.
exclusions: Jaw closure, a brief pinch, brushing, or a nudge without sustained control does not establish holding.
Later loss of the grasp does not erase this historical milestone.

stages.name: Align with the left clip (first)
stages.description: The held rope is brought into an insertion-ready orientation at the LEFT (FIRST) clip.
entryCriteria: The controlled rope is at the LEFT (FIRST) clip mouth region.
The local rope segment is visibly oriented with that clip's insertion axis, primarily verified in WRIST-L.
exclusions: Alignment far from the clip, empty-gripper alignment, and side-view overlap are insufficient.
No separate reach-the-clip stage or unengaged dwell interval is required.

stages.name: Engage the left clip (first)
stages.description: The rope itself engages the LEFT (FIRST) clip mouth in an insertion-directed interaction.
entryCriteria: The rope visibly contacts and begins entering under or into the LEFT (FIRST) clip lip, including partial insertion.
exclusions: Contact with the table, the clip exterior, or the gripper alone does not establish engagement.
Engagement does not prove a persistent seat; seating remains a separate physical judgment.

stages.name: First release
stages.description: The gripper lets go of the rope after the first-clip placement attempt.
entryCriteria: A previously held rope segment becomes free of the jaws as they open or separate from it after work at the LEFT (FIRST) clip.
Timestamp the first supported loss of gripper retention, not merely the start of jaw opening.
exclusions: The FIRST clip need not be successfully seated; this milestone records release, not placement quality.
An accidental slip from closed jaws or opening empty jaws is not a release.
A release during an initial pickup retry, before work at the FIRST clip, is not S5.
If this is also the episode's last release, it is still S5, not S10.

stages.name: Reach the rope again
stages.description: After the first-clip attempt, the gripper returns to the rope for the second pickup cycle.
entryCriteria: A distinct return to the rope after work at the LEFT (FIRST) clip brings the gripper within grasping range of the segment to be acquired for the RIGHT (SECOND) clip.
exclusions: The first clip does not need to be seated for the second cycle to begin.
Repeated grasp attempts before work at the FIRST clip remain first-cycle retries, not S6.
Continuing to transport the original held segment is not a new reach-to-pickup milestone.
Do not fabricate an earlier first-release timestamp if it was occluded.

stages.name: Hold the rope again
stages.description: The second pickup establishes a new secure, controlled hold of the rope.
entryCriteria: A distinct second acquisition after the first-clip attempt establishes sustained gripper-coupled rope motion across a visible interval.
The new hold may be on the same or a different rope segment.
exclusions: A missed close, transient pinch, or continuing the unchanged first hold is not S7.
The FIRST clip need not be seated; do not infer its state from the new grasp.

stages.name: Align with the right clip (second)
stages.description: The held rope is brought into an insertion-ready orientation at the RIGHT (SECOND) clip.
entryCriteria: The controlled rope is at the RIGHT (SECOND) clip mouth region.
WRIST-L positively establishes insertion-compatible orientation of the local rope segment relative to this clip.
exclusions: The FIRST clip need not remain seated; second-cycle progress and first-clip outcome are separate.
Orientation while far from the clip, empty-gripper alignment, or projection overlap is insufficient.
If the rope was carried continuously between clips, do not invent S6 or S7.

stages.name: Engage the right clip (second)
stages.description: The rope itself engages the RIGHT (SECOND) clip mouth in an insertion-directed interaction.
entryCriteria: The rope visibly contacts and begins entering under or into the RIGHT (SECOND) clip lip, including partial insertion.
exclusions: Engagement is not proof that either clip is fully seated.
Gripper-only contact, table contact, and merely hovering over the mouth are insufficient.
Do not require a successful first-clip seat to record an observed second-clip engagement.

stages.name: Final release
stages.description: The gripper lets go of the rope at the end of the second-clip placement attempt.
entryCriteria: A previously held rope segment becomes free of the opening or separating jaws after work at the RIGHT (SECOND) clip.
This is the final relinquishment of the routing attempt, not a temporary release followed by another pickup in that attempt.
exclusions: Release does not establish success: either clip may still be unseated.
Opening empty jaws or an accidental slip from closed jaws does not establish S10.
Ending the episode after only the first-clip release remains S5, not S10.
Timestamp actual loss of retention; do not wait for the gripper to retreat fully.

keyActions.name: Acquire controlled rope grasp
keyActions.description: A rope segment becomes visibly held and controlled: across a visible interval it moves coherently with the closed gripper and is lifted, tensioned, or translated.
keyActions.stageRelation: Required for observed first or second controlled-hold milestones; record the earliest genuine grasp independently of cycle.

keyActions.name: Reach left clip mouth region
keyActions.description: The controlled rope itself first reaches the canonical LEFT (FIRST) clip mouth region. Arrival does not by itself prove alignment, engagement, or seating.
keyActions.stageRelation: Supports first-clip alignment or engagement; clip arrival remains a key action, not an extra human stage.

keyActions.name: Seat rope in left clip
keyActions.description: The rope is first positively captured under or into the LEFT (FIRST) clip mouth and the capture persists long enough to establish a genuine seat; preserve this historical occurrence if the seat is later lost.
keyActions.stageRelation: Independent seating judgment required for task success. No stage, including the first release, proves this action.

keyActions.name: Release and re-grasp rope
keyActions.description: After releasing a previously controlled rope segment, the jaws acquire the same or another segment and establish a new controlled hold with sustained gripper-coupled motion.
keyActions.stageRelation: Supports S7 when this is the second pickup after the first-clip attempt; initial pickup retries do not establish the second cycle.

keyActions.name: Reach right clip mouth region
keyActions.description: The controlled rope itself first reaches the canonical RIGHT (SECOND) clip mouth region. Arrival does not by itself prove alignment, engagement, or seating.
keyActions.stageRelation: Supports second-clip alignment or engagement; clip arrival remains a key action, not an extra human stage.

keyActions.name: Attempt insertion at the right clip
keyActions.description: The controlled rope begins a deliberate insertion-directed movement into or against the RIGHT clip mouth. Includes missed entry. Mere arrival, alignment, passing nearby, accidental brushing, and screen overlap are not an insertion attempt. Record even if it precedes LEFT seating.
keyActions.stageRelation: Independent action for the left-before-right rule. Right-clip engagement necessarily involves an insertion attempt; do not rename it as work at the left clip.

keyActions.name: Seat rope in right clip
keyActions.description: The rope is first positively captured under or into the RIGHT (SECOND) clip mouth and the capture persists long enough to establish a genuine seat; record it honestly even if it occurs before the first-clip seat.
keyActions.stageRelation: Independent seating judgment required for task success. Second-clip engagement or final release alone does not prove this action.

keyActions.name: Terminally release rope
keyActions.description: At episode end the gripper lets go and leaves the rope in its final physical state; a temporary mid-task release followed by re-grasp is not this terminal action.
keyActions.stageRelation: Required for S10 final release after the second-clip attempt. A terminal release ending only the first cycle remains S5 and does not imply S10.

failureModes.description: No unresolved task failure; use for success. Recovered failure events may remain.

failureModes.name: Wrong clip order (right before left)
failureModes.description: A deliberate insertion attempt at the fixed RIGHT clip begins before the LEFT clip has been fully seated. This is a terminal, unrecoverable episode failure; later seating of either or both clips does not repair it. Use as primary failure ahead of all other causes, at the first violating right-clip attempt. Mere approach or overlap is not enough. If left seating/order is occluded, request review rather than treating not observed as proven absent.

No secure control of the rope is established in the relevant grasp sequence. A missed close, momentary pinch, or immediate escape without sustained control belongs here, not grasp_lost. A later secure grasp recovers this event.

The gripper establishes sustained control of the rope, then visibly loses it before correct placement. Excludes a momentary unsuccessful pinch, deliberate release, and loss of an already completed placement. A subsequent secure regrasp recovers this event.
After acquisition, no interaction attempt at the LEFT (FIRST) clip occurs before the recording ends. Use only when no more specific unrecovered grasp or clip failure is visible.
failureModes.name: Left clip · not attempted

failureModes.description: An actual interaction attempt at the LEFT (FIRST) clip does not enter beneath/into its retaining feature. Mere approach or overlap is insufficient. Subsequent real engagement recovers this event.
failureModes.name: Left clip · entry missed

failureModes.description: Rope enters the LEFT (FIRST) clip but does not become properly captured. Gripper release is not required. Subsequent secure seating recovers this event.
failureModes.name: Left clip · not fully seated

failureModes.description: Rope is positively seated in the LEFT (FIRST) clip, then visibly comes out. This is not a missed initial engagement. Subsequent restored seating recovers this event.
failureModes.name: Left clip · seated rope came out

failureModes.description: After acquisition, no interaction attempt at the RIGHT (SECOND) clip occurs before the recording ends. Use only when no more specific unrecovered grasp or clip failure is visible.
failureModes.name: Right clip · not attempted

failureModes.description: An actual interaction attempt at the RIGHT (SECOND) clip does not enter beneath/into its retaining feature. Mere approach or overlap is insufficient. Subsequent real engagement recovers this event.
failureModes.name: Right clip · entry missed

failureModes.description: Rope enters the RIGHT (SECOND) clip but does not become properly captured. Gripper release is not required. Subsequent secure seating recovers this event.
failureModes.name: Right clip · not fully seated

failureModes.description: Rope is positively seated in the RIGHT (SECOND) clip, then visibly comes out. This is not a missed initial engagement. Subsequent restored seating recovers this event.
failureModes.name: Right clip · seated rope came out

failureModes.description: Failure is known but the video cannot distinguish an observable category. Assess at the final decisive frame, set needs_human_review=true, and explain the missing evidence; do not invent a cause.

decisionRules.rule: FIRST means the fixed LEFT physical clip and SECOND means the fixed RIGHT physical clip in the canonical workspace frame. Opposing side cameras reverse apparent screen positions. Establish identity jointly from both views; never relabel the clip visited first as FIRST. If identity is unresolved, request human review.

LEFT seating must be achieved before the first deliberate RIGHT insertion attempt. Record wrong_clip_order at the first violating attempt; it is terminal across the whole episode, including retries. Later completion cannot recover it. Merely approaching or aligning with RIGHT is not an attempt. Preserve true physical actions and supported stages but never credit RIGHT work as LEFT progress. Missing visibility of LEFT seating alone is not proof of wrong order; flag unresolved order.

Use SIDE-1 and SIDE-2 together for global rope motion, controlled grasp, active-clip identity, and routing history. Use WRIST-L as the primary authority for local rope-versus-mouth orientation, lip engagement, and capture. A wrist close-up cannot override a side-view grasp miss, and side overlap cannot override a clear wrist non-seat.

The nominal stage sequence is S1 reach rope, S2 hold rope, S3 align at FIRST clip, S4 engage FIRST clip, S5 first-cycle release, then S6 reach rope again, S7 hold rope again, S8 align at SECOND clip, S9 engage SECOND clip, S10 final release. These are workflow milestones, not counts of seated clips. A failed first placement does not prevent credit for genuinely observed second-cycle milestones.

For S1 and S6, reach means arrival within grasping range of the rope segment, not the beginning of a distant approach. Timestamp the earliest supported arrival. Contact is not required. Distinguish the second acquisition from repeated first-pickup attempts using the intervening first-clip work.

Credit S2 or S7 only after sustained gripper-coupled control of a rope segment through lift, tension, or translation is visible. Do not depend on a fixed sampled-frame count. Timestamp the beginning of the confirmed hold. Jaw closure, a momentary pinch, proximity, and later arm travel do not prove retention. S7 requires a new acquisition, not merely continuing the first hold.

For S3/S8, require the held rope at the named clip mouth region with insertion-compatible local orientation. Use WRIST-L for fine geometry and both side views for clip identity and actual rope control. Do not add a separate clip-reach stage or require an unengaged dwell before crediting alignment.

For S4/S9, require positive rope entry or insertion-directed engagement under or into the named clip mouth. Table contact, clip exterior contact, empty-gripper proximity, or projection overlap is insufficient. Engagement is a stage even if it never becomes a persistent seat.

S5 is the first-cycle release after work at the FIRST clip; S10 is the final release after work at the SECOND clip. Credit actual relinquishment from opening or separating jaws, not an accidental slip or an empty-gripper opening. The first release does not become S10 merely because recording ends. Either release can occur after an unsuccessful placement; never infer seating from release.

S6/S7 mark return to the rope and renewed control for the second cycle. Neither requires a successful first-clip seat. A continuously held transfer may support S8/S9 without a separately observed S6/S7; do not invent a re-grasp. A retry before any first-clip work belongs to the first pickup, not the second cycle.

A clip is seated only when rope is positively visible captured under or into its mouth and capture persists across frames. Mere approach, contact, pressure, hovering, or dwell is not seating. Unverified capture means unknown, not confirmed unseated; retain supported stages and flag uncertainty.

Stages are achieved milestones, not intentions or failures. Preserve historical maximum despite later loss. Emit only supported transitions; equal times and forward jumps are allowed. Do not invent skipped stages.

A supplied human binary outcome is authoritative, but proves no stage, action, or timestamp. If success is known but completion is unseen, including recording cutoff, preserve supported observations and request review. Never manufacture seating or automatically rewrite historical human outcomes. A supplied success that contradicts a positively observed terminal order violation is a data conflict requiring adjudication, not permission to erase that event or invent left-first evidence. Never mutate the source human record.

Keep all distinct observable failures and recoveries. A wrong_clip_order event is terminal and always the primary failure, even if an earlier grasp/clip failure exists or both clips are eventually seated. Its primary time is the first violating RIGHT attempt. Otherwise select the earliest specific unrecovered failure; generic absence/unknown applies only without such an event. Success uses none only when no terminal violation occurred.

Use first visible onset for a missed attempt or loss. For no-attempt, incomplete-placement, or unknown modes only established when recording ends, use the final decisive frame as assessment time, not causal onset. Primary mode/time must match an event.

Occlusion is not evidence of failed grasp, absent engagement, or a drop. Use unknown_failure_cause and request review for unresolved failure evidence. Position and rotation misalignment are not separate categories.

A new attempt begins after the prior manipulation sequence is abandoned and a fresh acquisition sequence starts. Local insertion corrections, pauses, and occlusion do not create attempts. The planned second routing grasp belongs to the same two-clip attempt.

Timestamp the earliest supported achievement, not the start of trying. Secure grasp requires sustained object control across a visible interval, not a fixed number of sampled frames or momentary pinch. Use coupled motion and retention; request review if sparse evidence cannot resolve it.

No final-state enum or end-state output field exists in this protocol. Judge outcome from physical success criteria and any supplied human outcome. Release is optional. Later loss of correct placement before recording ends invalidates visually judged success. Correct placement is necessary but not sufficient: left-before-right ordering is mandatory.

auditProcedure: Identify the fixed LEFT/FIRST and RIGHT/SECOND clips using both side views before labeling stages.
Record achieved milestones and supported timestamps; later loss does not erase history.
Record independent key actions, including optional releases.
Check LEFT seating before every deliberate RIGHT insertion attempt. Record terminal wrong_clip_order first in primary-failure priority; otherwise select the earliest unrecovered specific failure.
Judge correct placement without requiring release. Preserve supplied human outcome and flag missing visual evidence.
Return trajectory-label/v2 without end-state fields. Check IDs, timing, stage/action consistency, and primary/event agreement.
